items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: I know that Herb Jeffries, I had a chance to work with him when I was working with Panama Francis up in the Rainbow Room.

ctx.x: Let me ask you one other thing, is you know we talked to a lot of jazz artists and in their own ways, in their own words they, many of them confirm that there is a type of spirituality in this music. In other words the music is more than just the technical ability to move fast over the keys.

Yeah. It’s, I believe that it’s a language and that the notes and all the things you learn, the exercises, the calisthenics, over the years are basically just the framework of the language, and once you learn how to manipulate that, like the alphabet and sentence structure, and that’s comparable in music as the different modes and all the intervals, which are the building blocks of the music, that’s what you’re able to pick. You know if you do a rising line, that brings a certain feeling or if you drop your line…

communication. So I believe that that sublimated into the instruments and so this communication is sort of the underlying thing about the instruments. Because I know I feel there is something that you know when I’m blowing, I get something off your chest, you know when you’re playing, that you really can’t put into words. But when you’re playing an instrument, after you’re done you feel satisfied like if you said something you needed to say that day you know? And I know depending on how I feel, my instrument lets…
